rounds.proof_sketch: Fixed input shape [16, 16384] → size = 16 * 16384 = 262,144. Kernel dispatch condition: if (size >= 1024) uses vectorized kernel, else uses scalar kernel. Since 262,144 >= 1024, the vectorized path is ALWAYS taken. The mutation is on line 78 inside the else branch (scalar path), which is never executed for this input size.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation modifies the num_blocks calculation specifically in the scalar kernel launch path, but this code path is only executed when size < 1024. With the fixed input shape of [16, 16384], the total element count is 262,144, which always satisfies the condition size >= 1024, causing the vectorized kernel path to be taken instead. The scalar kernel path containing the mutated line is dead code for this input configuration. No value-level test can change which kernel path is selected because the path selection logic depends solely on the tensor's element count (size), not on the numerical values within the tensor.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation resides in the scalar kernel path (else branch), which requires size < 1024 to execute. The fixed input shape [16, 16384] yields size = 262,144, guaranteeing the vectorized kernel path is always taken. Killing this mutant would require an input tensor with fewer than 1024 total elements, which violates the fixed-shape constraint.
rounds.recommendations: When designing mutation testing for GPU kernels with size-based dispatch (vectorized vs scalar paths), the test suite must include input configurations that exercise EACH code path independently. For this kernel, the test suite should include both (1) shapes with size >= 1024 to test the vectorized path, and (2) shapes with size < 1024 to test the scalar path. Without both, mutations in one path become inherently unkillable when testing with inputs that only trigger the other path.
